title: Yordan Alvarez out of Friday’s Astros lineup after ankle scare
content:
ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. — Amid his plateauing pursuit of a Triple Crown and after turning his right ankle on Thursday afternoon, Houston Astros designated hitter Yordan Alvarez isn’t in the lineup for Friday’s series opener against the Tampa Bay Rays — a rarity within his remarkable season.

Alvarez had started 145 of the Astros’ first 147 games. He has already taken a career-high 637 plate appearances, across which Alvarez has authored one of the best offensive seasons in Astros history.

It has slowed somewhat since the All-Star break, with Alvarez losing his place atop both the American League home run and RBI leaderboards. Tampa Bay third baseman Junior Caminero entered Friday with 39 home runs, one more than Alvarez, while Baltimore first baseman Pete Alonso’s 97 RBIs also put him one ahead.

Alvarez has hit just three home runs since July 29, a span of 38 games in which he still has a .405 on-base percentage and .830 OPS. It’s hard to call that a slump, but given the expectations around Alvarez, it qualifies.

On Friday, manager Joe Espada said Alvarez’s absence from the starting lineup stemmed from an ankle turn during the eighth inning of Thursday’s 2-1 victory against the Philadelphia Phillies. Alvarez took an awkward step while jogging into third base and required a visit from the team’s athletic training staff.

Alvarez hit in the batting cages before Friday’s game at Tropicana Field and participated in some other pregame work in hopes of being available off the bench. Asked whether Alvarez underwent imaging, Espada said the team didn’t believe it was necessary.

“We want him in there,” Espada said. “He feels strong and feels really good, but an (off) day like today, especially on this turf, I think it will be beneficial for him.”

Alvarez’s .310 batting average is still best in the American League, though Tampa left fielder Chandler Simpson is close at .308. No major-league hitter has won a Triple Crown since Miguel Cabrera in 2012. If Alvarez can win it this season, he will be the first left-handed hitter to win a Triple Crown since Carl Yastrzemski in 1967.
